Andrew Mills clocked a snappy 10.4 for the 'dash' and Junior Tony Brooks ran a spirited 52.2 for the 440 yds but despite these and other good performances we were well and truly beaten by Walton to the tune of 59½ points.
Main points scorers have been John Kelly, Tony Brooks and Philip Gee - all first year Juniors, and Stevie White who is only a first year Youth and one of the most promising young athletes we have.
Tony Brooks took the 'quarter' comfortably in 54.2 having already competed in three field events plus the LAC Schools 44oy (53.0) the evening before.

A very good leg by Philip brought us to within reach of the leaders and on the next leg Tony Brooks caught up even more. Kevin Finn did well on the last stretch to pursue the leaders right to the finish but we could only manage 3rd place.
Our Junior team completely outclassed the opposition with Tony Brooks winning three events (all with good performances) and Philip Gee placing 2nd twice.

Consistently in the 52.0 sec. range, Tony Brooks looks set to do well in the more important championships lined up in the next few weeks. Yet again John Kelly had a duel with Hylands (Hercules) who was this time running as a guest, and once again he was just pipped, the rest of the field way back.

Another Belgrave team win with two individual firsts from John Kelly with the unlikely combination of Javelin and 880y(report elsewhere) and another double from Tony Brooks in the two longer sprints with further places in the Javelin and Long Jump.
Philip Gee romped both sprints with Tony Brooks giving us another 52.0 clocking in the 440yds. John Kelly added another string to his bow - this time the shot which he won together with the Javelin.

Jim Vivian took both sprints as expected from Philip Gee in the 100yds and Tony Brooks in the 220yds. Tony also won the 'quarter' and 'half' in good times with Philip 2nd again and John Hamilton, only a first year Youth, putting up a great performance for 3rd place in the shorter event.

Jim Vivian was beaten into 3rd place in the Junior furlong by the fast improving Alan Pascoe (Portsmouth AC) and L.Taylor (Guildford) who Jim beat in the 'Surrey'. The quarter-mile saw Tony Brooks putting up two very good times in qualifying for the final the following week.

Tony Brooks was the eventual winner in the fastest race with 62.0 secs. with Denzil Winsborrow, after falling, a close second. I am sure that three of the competitors for this event will break 60 seconds during the summer which will be very useful for our A & B strings in the National league.
